transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-13 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Anya Patel (CSM) -- Rajiv, Tessa, Ben, Marta (Catalyst)

Auto-summary: quick QBR/check-in. Focus on recent cost growth driven by new chat expansion, intermittent tail latency on late-night batch jobs, and a security ask around KMS and audit logs. Redwood suggests a weekend dedicated pilot and a stress test to nail 99.9.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. quick roll call - we have, uh, Diego and Anya from our side. maya here.
[00:06] Rajiv: hey thanks, yeah Rajiv here. hope you all are well. we'll be mostly focused on the cost spike and a couple of reliability incidents we saw last quarter.
[00:12] Tessa: Tessa here, i'll try to jump in with platform numbers.
[00:15] Ben: ben, s r e. saw the incidents.
[00:18] Marta: marta from security, i'll keep notes on compliance asks.
[00:22] Diego: hi, Diego Ruiz, Redwood SE. we'll kick off with a short data readout, then go into proposed mitigations.

[00:30] Maya: quick agenda: usage+cost trends, latency incidents and root cause hypotheses, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, security checklist, and then concrete next steps. sound ok?
[00:40] Rajiv: yes. let's go.

[01:02] Diego: okay pulling up the metrics we saw — summarizing at a high level: Catalyst's token volume has doubled month-over-month since the chat release, with peak QPS concentrated in the 02:00-05:00 UTC window. cost per effective request rose ~28% — mainly due to longer sequences and repeated full-context calls without prefix caching. some of the caching here looks cold — the K V cache hit rate is lower than expected.
[01:30] Tessa: yeah that's what we saw. our jobs do a lot of full context retrieval for multi-turn chat, and we also have a nightly batch that re-runs moderation checks which spiked.
[01:45] Rajiv: the modulation check — that batch was responsible for the spike on june 30th, correct?
[01:48] Diego: that's right. and we also observed a handful of 99.9th latency outliers during the same window; from tracing it looks like some requests hit a cold KV and then there was a model fallback to a slightly larger variant which added tokenization overhead.
[02:10] Ben: so fallback logic is in play. any way to reduce those fallbacks?
[02:14] Diego: yeah two levers — increase warm pool capacity or pin a cheaper model variant with more aggressive quantization for batch. the tradeoff is a small quality delta vs a big cost/latency win.
[02:30] Rajiv: quality delta is the problem. our NPS for the feature dropped when we switched. we need to set an SLO for user-visible drops.
[02:39] Maya: understood. one option we proposed before is a weekend Dedicated pool for heavy batch windows and keeping hosted API for daytime interactive traffic. you get isolation and predictable throughput for the batch jobs.
[02:52] Tessa: i like separation. does Redwood offer autoscale for dedicated pools? we don't want to overcommit.
[02:57] Diego: yes, dedicated has autoscaling policies and burst capacity; you can define a base commit and burst for episodic spikes. we can also suggest a policy that favors warm cache residency during the weekend window.
[03:12] Marta: from security perspective — if we move to Dedicated, what changes for keys and audit logs? we need KMS integration and proof of HSM-backed key handling. also, retention of request logs for 90 days in an audit-friendly format.
[03:28] Maya: good question. we integrate with customer KMS (both cloud KMS and HSM-backed). we also provide signed audit logs and per-token trace mappings that can be exported. i'll send the attestation packet.
[03:38] Marta: great, do you have SOC 2 or ISO docs updated recently?
[03:42] Maya: yes SOC 2 Type II; i'll attach the latest report and a short summary of what is covered.
[03:48] Rajiv: back to reliability — do you have suggestions on model quantization that retain our prompt quality? we can't accept hallucinations.
[03:55] Diego: yes, we have quantization profiles tuned per-model and per-workload. the SE team can recommend a profile that reduces memory/latency with minimal ROUGE/accuracy regression. we often run A/B for ~10k samples to validate.
[04:10] Tessa: can Redwood run a benchmark with our prompts? we can provide a representative prompt set.
[04:14] Diego: absolutely, that's part of the stress bench we usually run. we collect latency distributions and quality metrics.
[04:20] Rajiv: what's the typical timeline for that bench?
[04:23] Diego: we can spin up a 4-hour bench in pre-prod within a week if schedules align. results normally within 48 hours after run.
[04:30] Maya: action item: we'll propose a few run windows; do you have preferred dates?
[04:34] Tessa: weekends are better, between 02:00-06:00 UTC.
[04:38] Ben: i want to see the 99.9th and how much KV miss is driving it.
[04:42] Diego: we'll include KV hit histograms and per-request fallbacks.
[04:46] Rajiv: about costs — can you break down the 28% increase? was it mostly token count or model selection?
[04:52] Diego: most of it is longer average sequence length and repeated full context calls. some of it is that the moderation batch used a larger variant and had lower cache locality. we've got an annotated spreadsheet we'll send showing per-route token delta.
[05:06] Maya: i'll send the cost breakdown with per-route guidance and some knobs you can flip — e.g., prefix caching, partial context, and model pinning.
[05:12] Tessa: regarding pinning, what's the rollback path if quality drops?
[05:16] Diego: rollouts can be canaryed; Redwood supports traffic split and automatic fallback policies to revert to hosted default model if errors exceed thresholds.
[05:26] Rajiv: can we set a guardrail where if human-visible error > x% we automatically revert?
[05:30] Anya: yes, we can tie quality regression alerts to prompt eval sets; if performance regresses on that eval set beyond threshold, the system triggers alert and optional rollback.
[05:40] Marta: any concerns about data residency if we use dedicated in a shared region? we need EU residency for certain PII routes.
[05:46] Maya: you can pin dedicated capacity to a region and we support VPC/private deployments for stricter residency.
[05:52] Tessa: timeline question — if we commit to a dedicated weekend slot, how long to provision?
[05:56] Diego: if commit is approved, we can provision a dedicated pool in ~7 business days for standard configurations; expedited for enterprise deals with a small provisioning surcharge.
[06:08] Rajiv: fine. cost sensitivity — we prefer a 3 month pilot rather than an annual commit.
[06:12] Maya: that works, we can offer a pilot with a trimmed commit and a clear exit.
[06:18] Ben: what about autoscaling limits? i want to cap potential runaway costs during an incident.
[06:22] Diego: you can set hard caps and alerting thresholds; plus we support token-level rate limiting per route.
[06:28] Tessa: on the monitoring side, can we get per-route token-level cost attribution in the console?
[06:33] Anya: yes, Console exposes per-route cost & latency and token breakdown; we can export a CSV for your finance team.
[06:40] Rajiv: good. any competitors we should be aware of? we benchmarked LambdaCloud for raw price but quality was lower and tool integrations were missing.
[06:48] Maya: noted. our historical win is on predictable tail latency and observability.
[06:53] Diego: just to highlight technical mitigation options as a quick checklist: 1) weekend dedicated pool with warm cache residency, 2) model pinning+quantization for batch, 3) smarter prefix caching, 4) fallback tuning and canary + eval-based rollback.
[07:12] Tessa: that checklist seems actionable. can you guys document recommended knobs for each route?
[07:17] Diego: yes we'll annotate per-route recommendations.
[07:20] Maya: okay let's recap and write action items.
[07:24] Maya: Diego will schedule stress bench for a weekend slot and include KV histograms and latency percentiles.
[07:30] Diego: i'll aim for 2027-07-22 as the first run, pending Catalyst confirmation.
[07:34] Maya: i'll send the cost breakdown sheet and the SOC2/KMS attestation bundle by 2027-07-16.
[07:40] Tessa: i'll push platform traffic patterns and cache-hit metrics by 2027-07-15.
[07:45] Marta: i'll share required security questionnaire answers by 2027-07-18.
[07:50] Rajiv: after the bench, schedule follow-up the week of 2027-07-25 to go over results and pilot terms.
[07:56] Maya: perfect. any final Qs?
[07:59] Ben: none from me.
[08:02] Tessa: nope.
[08:04] Rajiv: thanks everyone.
[08:07] Maya: thanks all. we'll follow up.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (K V cache noted as K V cash in the raw audio), speaker overlap around 05:30-06:00 where there was light crosstalk.

References shared: cost_breakdown_catalyst_v1.xlsx (link in Fireflies notes), SOC2_Attestation_June2027.pdf (link), proposed_dedicated_pricing_preview.pdf (link).

End of transcript.
